stated: Reform UK will abolish the VAT refund scheme for tourist shopping, which they claim has cost the economy over £10 billion and deterred up to 2 million tourists.

source.quote: Abolish the VAT Tourist Tax The government has cost our economy over £10 billion when they stopped the VAT refund scheme for tourist shopping. This also deterred up to 2 million tourists.

bearing_set.reason: Restoring VAT-free shopping for overseas visitors is projected to materially boost tourist retail and hospitality spending, with direct employment and earnings effects for workers in the UK's sizable retail and tourism sectors — a real, non-negligible job-creation verdict.

Reinstating VAT refunds for tourist shoppers is argued (CEBR) to boost inbound retail spending and tourism GDP; the credible counter (OBR/Treasury) is that the original removal was broadly revenue-neutral on activity — a genuine contested forecast about real living standards and business dynamism.

Restoring the scheme directly reduces VAT receipts on tourist purchases; Treasury estimated the old scheme's net fiscal cost in the hundreds of millions per year, making this a material funded-vs-unfunded question on the debt path.

membership_note: The two fundamentals are the classic efficiency-vs-fiscal-cost tradeoff here: O13 (does more tourist spending outweigh lost VAT?), O12 (the revenue foregone must be accounted for). No material effect on UK residents' own tax burden (O11), cost of essentials (O2), or other fundamentals.
